dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the capabilities: create short links, read analytics, list/edit/delete links, and optionally compose QR/chart outputs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill clearly describes PicSee MCP endpoints, OAuth, tool names, and scopes; optional QR/chart recipes use third-party services and are disclosed most clearly in the Skill Card rather than inline in each recipe.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is configuration-only for MCP clients, with optional npx mcp-remote bridge usage for clients without remote MCP support; no packaged executable skill code is present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Outbound access to PicSee is necessary for a URL shortener, and optional api.qrserver.com/quickchart.io calls are purpose-aligned but may expose short links or analytics data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill itself does not store credentials, but authenticated use grants user:read and user:write through the MCP client, allowing edits or deletion of account links after OAuth approval.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: The rm cleanup commands are manual migration instructions for old PicSee v2 artifacts, not automatic behavior; they are scoped but should be reviewed before use.
[SQP-2] expected: QR generation via api.qrserver.com is an optional client-side recipe; the third-party egress is real and disclosed in the Skill Card.
[SQP-2] expected: QuickChart chart rendering is optional and purpose-aligned for analytics visualization, but users should avoid it for sensitive analytics.
[E1] expected: Sending destination URLs and analytics to PicSee is inherent to the service, and the artifact warns that sensitive URLs should not be shortened.
[TM1] expected: The flagged rm -rf commands are documentation-only cleanup steps for specific old skill CLI directories, not tool-parameter abuse in executable code.
[YR1] expected: The YARA hit is explained by scoped migration cleanup commands and unrelated wording about token refresh; no malware payload or autonomous destructive action was found.
llm.guidance: Install only if you trust PicSee with the destination URLs and analytics you ask it to process. Do not shorten URLs containing secrets, tokens, or private query parameters; confirm before letting an agent edit or delete links; and review the migration cleanup commands carefully before running them.
llm.summary: This documentation-only skill connects agents to PicSee for URL shortening and link analytics, with expected but important privacy and account-control risks disclosed.
